items.title: 9.2 Lewis concept of acids and bases

source_refs.note: Topic 9.2, printed page 191. The printed adduct drawings are described, not reproduced.

blocks.text: In 1923 G. N. Lewis proposed a generalised definition of acid-base behaviour in which acids and bases are identified by their ability to accept or donate a pair of electrons and form a coordinate covalent bond.

blocks.title: Lewis acid and base
blocks.text: A Lewis acid is any species (molecule or ion) that can accept a pair of electrons, and a Lewis base is any species (molecule or ion) that can donate a pair of electrons. A Lewis acid-base reaction occurs when a base donates a pair of electrons to an acid.

In the reaction of silver ion with ammonia, each of two ammonia molecules (Lewis bases) donates a pair of electrons to the positively charged silver ion (the Lewis acid), giving the adduct [H3N-Ag-NH3]+. The sum of the charges on the left is +1, so the acid-base adduct on the right must carry a charge of +1.

The boron atom in boron trifluoride, BF3, has only six electrons in its valence shell. With an incomplete octet it behaves as an electron-pair acceptor, so BF3 is a very good Lewis acid and reacts with many Lewis bases. With a fluoride ion as the base, donating one of its lone pairs, the adduct is BF4-; the sum of the charges on the left is -1, so the charge on the adduct is also -1.
Identify the Lewis acid and the Lewis base in the reactions of SO3 with O2-, HCl with H2O, and BF3 with NH3, writing the equations.
